metaDescription: Paete lanzones is a lanzones variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Paete is a registered lanzones variety, also sold or known as lansones Paete or Camiguin lanzones. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1991. IPB bred it.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for lansones Paete or Camiguin lanzones, this is the same lanzones. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [lanzones variety finder](/crop-varieties/lanzones), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.
The pests and diseases that hit lanzones fields most often: [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A fruit of Paete weighs about 16 grams, and its shape is oblong. The flesh is smooth and firm.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Bunches of 15 to 25, fruit about 3.2 to 3.4 cm, about 16 g, oblong, yellow, almost seedless (0 to 2), thin skin with latex even when ripe, about 16 Brix.
Registered in 1991 with the Philippine Seed Board.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the most commonly grown lanzones, named after Paete, Laguna, a specialty of Camiguin, Gingoog and Laguna. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Paete lanzones

Paete and Camiguin lanzones are prized for sweet, seedless segments. Plant grafted trees, which bear years sooner than seedlings. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is lansones Paete the same as Paete?
items.a: Yes. lansones Paete is another name for Paete. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Paete?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
